title: Client Connector performance runbook: MTU, Path MTU Discovery and the temporary Z-Tunnel 1.0 fallback

mtu-discovery-dtls-only.statement: Path MTU Discovery applies only to DTLS mode; in TLS mode TCP negotiates the MSS for the outer connection automatically, and the runbook says to skip its MTU section if Path MTU Discovery is enabled in the forwarding profile for DTLS.

quotes: MTU Discovery is only applicable for DTLS mode. In the case of TLS mode, TCP negotiates the Maximum Segment Size (MSS) for the outer connection automatically.
Skip this section if you have enabled the Path MTU Discovery option for DTLS mode in the forwarding profile.

dtls-default-mtu-mss.statement: In DTLS Z-Tunnel 2.0 mode the default MTU is 1400 and the MSS is MTU - 40 = 1360; in TLS, Client Connector is not involved in MSS.

quotes: In the case of DTLS Tunnel 2.0 mode, the default MTU value is 1400. Consequently, the MSS value is MTU - 40 = 1360.
In the case of TLS, TCP negotiates the MSS for the outer connection automatically. Zscaler Client Connector is not involved in making it work.

mtu-local-page.statement: To change MTU from the local page, enable Allow end user to override Z-Tunnel 2.0 or ZPA protocol settings, browse to http://127.0.0.1:9000/zconfig?q=@<CustomerDomain>, select a value under MTU, and click Restart Service in the More window.

quotes: enable Allow end user to override Z-Tunnel 2.0 or ZPA protocol settings.
direct the user to browse to http://127.0.0.1:9000/zconfig?q=@<CustomerDomain>
select one of the available values under MTU as shown in the following image:
To enable these changes, click Restart Service in the More window of Zscaler Client Connector.

mtu-profile.statement: The profile route to MTU testing sets MTU for Zscaler Adapter to less than 1400, preferably in increments of 50, in a new forwarding profile; the user then clicks Update Policy.

quotes: In the new forwarding profile, under the MTU for Zscaler Adapter, configure an MTU size less than 1400 (preferably in increments of 50).
Users must then click Update Policy in Zscaler Client Connector to get assigned to the new profile.

mtu-improvement-meaning.statement: If performance improves after an MTU below 1400 is set for the Zscaler Adapter, the runbook says a hop in the path has a smaller MTU, fragmenting Client Connector packets; the options are to report to the ISP or keep the value, or enable Path MTU Discovery in the forwarding profile.

quotes: under the MTU for Zscaler Adapter, configure an MTU size less than 1400 (preferably in increments of 50).

If the performance improves, this means that one of the hops in the path has less MTU size, thereby fragmenting the packets originating from Zscaler Client Connector and leading to performance degradation.
You can either report this problem to the ISP and get this issue rectified or continue using this value which is determined to be optimal.
you can enable the Path MTU Discovery option in the forwarding profile, which enables Zscaler Client Connector to automatically determine the path MTU.

ztunnel1-fallback.statement: If MTU changes do not help, the runbook says to switch to Z-Tunnel 1.0 for testing and data gathering; this is not a permanent solution, MTU modification is for testing only, and Z-Tunnel 1.0 cannot intercept non-web traffic.

quotes: If there is no improvement in performance, switch to Z-Tunnel 1.0 to perform some tests and data gathering.
The workaround is not recommended as a permanent solution. Modifying the MTU size is only for testing purposes.
Switching to Z-Tunnel 1.0 means Zscaler Client Connector is incapable of intercepting non-web traffic.

switch-to-ztunnel1-steps.statement: To switch temporarily to Z-Tunnel 1.0, select the Z-Tunnel 1.0 option under Forwarding Profile Action for Internet & SaaS in the new forwarding profile; the user then clicks Update Policy.

quotes: In the new forwarding profile, under Forwarding Profile Action for Internet & SaaS, select the Z-Tunnel 1.0 option.
Click Update Policy on Zscaler Client Connector to be assigned to the new profile.

default-mtu-behind-tunnels.summary: The runbook gives 1400 as the default MTU in DTLS Z-Tunnel 2.0 mode without qualification; the forwarding profile page gives 1400 for a direct connection and 1360 or 1300 behind GRE or IPSec tunnels.

quotes: In the case of DTLS Tunnel 2.0 mode, the default MTU value is 1400. Consequently, the MSS value is MTU - 40 = 1360.

positions.says: The default MTU in DTLS Z-Tunnel 2.0 mode is 1400, and the MSS is 1360.

quotes: The default value for a direct connection is 1400 and 1360/1300 for GRE/IPSec tunnels, respectively.

positions.says: The default MTU is 1400 for a direct connection and 1360 or 1300 for GRE or IPSec tunnels.

default-mtu-behind-tunnels.impact: Behind a GRE or IPSec tunnel the default to test against, and the MSS the runbook derives from it, differ by which page is read; see zcc.z-tunnel.transport:mtu.

keep-mtu-vs-testing-only.summary: On the same runbook page, a smaller MTU that improves performance can be kept as the optimal value, while the later fallback text says modifying the MTU size is only for testing purposes and not a permanent solution.

quotes: You can either report this problem to the ISP and get this issue rectified or continue using this value which is determined to be optimal.

positions.says: If a smaller MTU improves performance, the user can continue using that value.

quotes: The workaround is not recommended as a permanent solution. Modifying the MTU size is only for testing purposes.

positions.says: Modifying the MTU size is only for testing and the workaround is not recommended as a permanent solution.

keep-mtu-vs-testing-only.impact: Whether a working reduced MTU can stay in a production forwarding profile depends on which sentence is read; the page also offers Path MTU Discovery as the alternative.

mtu-test-value.title: Which MTU values the runbook expects to try below 1400
mtu-test-value.detail: The runbook says to configure an MTU size less than 1400, preferably in increments of 50, and gives no starting value or lower bound. The forwarding profile page gives a range of 800 to 1400 (1300 to 1400 for IPv6) for the MTU for Zscaler Adapter setting (see [[zcc.z-tunnel.transport]]); neither page says where in that range to start.
